su-su-xao-ca-rot.name: Chayote Stir-Fried with Carrot
su-su-xao-ca-rot.serving_basis: A dish for four people at a Vietnamese family meal.
su-su-xao-ca-rot.description: Crisp chayote is quickly stir-fried with carrot strips, garlic, and light seasoning. This colorful vegetable dish pairs easily with a braise or a vegetarian rice meal.
su-su-xao-ca-rot.finished_dish: The chayote and carrot are just tender with a slight crispness; the garlic is fragrant and little liquid remains.
su-su-xao-ca-rot.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice as a vegetable dish.
tips: Cut the vegetables into even strips so they cook at the same pace.
Stir-fry over high heat; add water a spoonful at a time if the pan dries out.
Season lightly first and adjust once the vegetables soften.
su-su-xao-ca-rot.image_alt: A quick vegetable stir-fry made with chayote, carrot, and garlic.
su-su-xao-ca-rot.media_alt_text: A quick vegetable stir-fry made with chayote, carrot, and garlic.
su-su-xao-ca-rot.time_note: About 25 minutes, including preparation and cooking.

ingredients.name: Chayote
ingredients.notes: Peel, remove mature seeds if present, and cut into even strips.

ingredients.name: Carrot
ingredients.notes: Peel and cut into strips similar in size to the chayote.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.notes: Peeled and minced.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For saut?ing the garlic and vegetables.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Choose a product suitable for a vegetarian diet; add gradually.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Adjust to taste.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Optional.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Add a spoonful at a time only if needed.

preparation_steps: Peel and cut the chayote into even strips; remove mature seeds if present.
Peel and cut the carrot into similar strips. Peel and mince the garlic.
cooking_steps: Heat oil and sauté the garlic until fragrant without browning.
Add carrot, stir for 1 minute, then add chayote and stir-fry over high heat until beginning to soften.
Season with vegetarian seasoning and salt. Add water a spoonful at a time if needed and cook until just tender.
Taste, add pepper if using, and turn off the heat while the vegetables retain a slight crispness.

canh-bi-do-dau-phong-chay.name: Vegetarian Pumpkin and Peanut Soup
canh-bi-do-dau-phong-chay.serving_basis: A dish for four people at a Vietnamese family meal.
canh-bi-do-dau-phong-chay.description: Tender pumpkin and peanuts make a gently sweet vegetarian soup. These familiar ingredients suit a Vietnamese family meal.
canh-bi-do-dau-phong-chay.finished_dish: The pumpkin holds its shape, the peanuts are soft, and the broth is mildly sweet and lightly seasoned.
canh-bi-do-dau-phong-chay.serving: Serve hot with rice and other vegetarian dishes; finish with scallions and cilantro.
tips: Soak the peanuts first to help them soften evenly.
Add the pumpkin after the peanuts are nearly tender; cut it into even pieces.
Season lightly to preserve the pumpkin?s natural sweetness.
canh-bi-do-dau-phong-chay.image_alt: A gently sweet vegetarian soup of pumpkin, peanuts, and fresh herbs.
canh-bi-do-dau-phong-chay.media_alt_text: A gently sweet vegetarian soup of pumpkin, peanuts, and fresh herbs.
canh-bi-do-dau-phong-chay.time_note: About 75 minutes, including preparation and cooking.

ingredients.name: Pumpkin
ingredients.notes: Peeled, seeded, and cut into even pieces.

ingredients.name: Raw peanuts
ingredients.notes: Pick out damaged kernels, rinse, and soak for about 30 minutes.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: For the soup; some may be replaced with vegetable stock.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peeled and minced.

ingredients.name: Cooking oil
ingredients.notes: For saut?ing the shallot; may be omitted.

ingredients.name: Vegetarian seasoning powder
ingredients.notes: Choose a product suitable for a vegetarian diet.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Adjust after the pumpkin is cooked.

ingredients.name: Scallions
ingredients.notes: Rinsed and finely sliced.

ingredients.name: Cilantro
ingredients.notes: Rinsed and chopped for garnish.

preparation_steps: Rinse and soak peanuts for about 30 minutes, then drain.
Peel and seed the pumpkin, cut it into even pieces, and mince the shallot.
Rinse and chop the scallions and cilantro.
cooking_steps: Heat oil and sauté the shallot until fragrant; add the peanuts and stir briefly.
Add water, bring to a boil, then simmer until peanuts are nearly tender, skimming foam.
Add pumpkin and simmer until tender but not falling apart.
Season with vegetarian seasoning and salt. Taste, turn off the heat, and finish with scallions and cilantro.

canh-khoai-mo-chay-nam-dui-ga.name: Vegetarian Purple Yam Soup with King Oyster Mushrooms
aliases: Purple Yam and King Oyster Mushroom Soup
Vegetarian Purple Yam Soup with Mushrooms
canh-khoai-mo-chay-nam-dui-ga.serving_basis: A dish for four people at a Vietnamese family meal.
canh-khoai-mo-chay-nam-dui-ga.description: Grated purple yam and king oyster mushrooms make a gently thick vegetarian soup associated with southern Vietnamese home cooking.
canh-khoai-mo-chay-nam-dui-ga.finished_dish: The broth is naturally thick and pale purple; mushrooms are tender yet chewy, and the seasoning lets the yam remain prominent.
canh-khoai-mo-chay-nam-dui-ga.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice and finish with scallions and culantro.
tips: Grate the yam just before cooking; wear gloves if its sap irritates your skin.
Cut the mushrooms into bite-size pieces to retain their texture.
Add the yam gradually to the simmering broth while stirring gently.

preparation_steps: Peel, rinse, and grate the yam; gloves can help prevent irritation.
Wipe the mushrooms clean and slice them. Peel and mince the shallot.
Rinse and chop the scallions and culantro.
cooking_steps: Heat oil and sauté shallot until fragrant. Add mushrooms and stir for about 2 minutes.
Add water, bring to a boil, then simmer. Season with vegetarian seasoning, soy sauce, and salt.
Add grated yam in small portions while stirring gently; simmer 8–10 minutes until cooked and lightly thickened.
Taste, add scallions and culantro, and turn off the heat.

canh-ga-kho-gung.name: Chicken Wings Braised with Ginger
canh-ga-kho-gung.serving_basis: A dish for four people at a Vietnamese family meal.
canh-ga-kho-gung.description: Chicken wings are marinated with fish sauce, shallot, garlic, and ginger, then gently braised. A lightly reduced sauce and warm ginger aroma make this a familiar dish for rice.
canh-ga-kho-gung.finished_dish: The wings are fully cooked and tender without falling apart; a glossy brown sauce coats them with balanced savory and sweet notes.
canh-ga-kho-gung.serving: Serve hot with steamed rice, boiled vegetables, or a mild soup.
tips: Choose wings of similar size so they cook evenly.
Marinate under refrigeration, then let the chicken lose its chill before cooking.
Braise gently and turn carefully; add hot water if the sauce reduces too quickly.
canh-ga-kho-gung.image_alt: Vietnamese ginger-braised chicken wings with a glossy sauce.
canh-ga-kho-gung.media_alt_text: Vietnamese ginger-braised chicken wings with a glossy sauce.
canh-ga-kho-gung.time_note: About 75 minutes, including preparation and cooking.

ingredients.notes: Cut into serving pieces, rinse, and drain well.

ingredients.name: Fresh ginger
ingredients.notes: Peel; slice half and mince the rest.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: Peeled and minced.

ingredients.notes: Peeled and minced.

ingredients.name: Fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Adjust to its saltiness.

ingredients.notes: For seasoning and a light caramel color.

ingredients.notes: Reduce if caramelizing sugar directly.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Optional; reduce for a milder dish.

ingredients.name: Scallions

preparation_steps: Rinse, cut, and drain the wings. Peel the ginger; slice half and mince the rest.
Refrigerate the wings for 15 minutes with fish sauce, half the aromatics, minced ginger, pepper, and some sugar.
Mince the remaining shallot and garlic; rinse and slice the scallions.
cooking_steps: Sauté the remaining aromatics in oil. Cook sugar to a light caramel color, or use caramel sauce.
Add the wings and sear until firm. Add sliced ginger, the marinade, and hot water.
Bring to a boil, lower the heat, partly cover, and braise 25–30 minutes, turning once. Add a little hot water if needed.
Adjust seasoning and continue until fully cooked with a lightly coating sauce. Finish with scallions.

canh-ga-nam.name: Chicken and Mushroom Soup
aliases: Chicken Soup with King Oyster Mushrooms
canh-ga-nam.serving_basis: A dish for four people at a Vietnamese family meal.
canh-ga-nam.description: Chicken simmers with king oyster mushrooms, carrot, and corn for a mild soup suited to a family meal. Gentle cooking keeps the chicken tender and the broth clear.
canh-ga-nam.finished_dish: The broth is clear and gently sweet; the chicken is tender, mushrooms are chewy, and vegetables are soft without falling apart.
canh-ga-nam.serving: Ladle hot and garnish with scallions and cilantro. Serve with steamed rice.
tips: Blanch the chicken first for a clearer broth, then rinse the pot before cooking.
Skim foam during a gentle simmer and avoid a vigorous boil.
Add mushrooms near the end so they remain chewy.

preparation_steps: Rinse and drain the chicken, then cut it into serving pieces.
Wipe and slice mushrooms. Peel and cut the carrot; slice the corn into rounds.
Peel and crush the shallot; rinse and chop the scallions and cilantro.
cooking_steps: Put chicken, water, shallot, and corn in a pot. Bring to a boil, skim foam, and reduce to a gentle simmer.
Simmer about 20 minutes, add carrot, and continue until chicken is nearly tender.
Add mushrooms and cook 7–10 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked and vegetables are just tender.
Season with fish sauce, salt, and seasoning powder. Taste, turn off the heat, and finish with herbs.
